summary: This video presents a landscape photographer’s foundational post-processing workflow using RAW in Camera Raw and Photoshop, with comparisons to Bridge and Lightroom, and a philosophy grounded in building a light source and fluid transitions through a scene. It covers RAW extraction of dynamic range, color and tonal adjustments, and a spectrum of Photoshop tools—from traditional adjustments (color balance, selective color) to advanced warping (Adaptive Wide Angle, Perspective Warp, Puppet Warp) and diffusion effects (Gaussian blur/Orton). The instructor emphasizes a non-destructive approach (layers, multiple saved versions, history painting) and two original techniques for painting adjustments (history paint and clone paint). Throughout, the emphasis is on understanding tool behavior, balancing color with tonal decisions, and practicing speed while maintaining image integrity without overreliance on any single “magic” tool.

sections.title: Intro: Tools and basic workflow
sections.description: Opening remarks about tool choice versus mastery, and the workflow context—opening a RAW in Photoshop and imagining it in Lightroom/Bridge to set expectations.

sections.title: RAW entry and cross-ecosystem workflow
sections.description: Discussion of how ACR sits between Lightroom and Photoshop, and why the presenter treats ACR as the quick RAW processor before moving edits into Photoshop; emphasis on not relying solely on previews load times and organizational systems.

sections.title: Color and tonal strategies in RAW vs Photoshop
concepts: early discussion of color grading vs HSL/Selective Color
sections.description: Explains how color decisions tie to light adjustments, introduces the idea that color grading and tonal changes operate on both color and luminance—with a preference toward selective color in certain scenarios and a caution about HSL in flat gradients.

sections.title: Tool landscape and cautions
sections.description: Survey of tools including AI-based tools, legacy Photoshop filters, and color filters, with cautions about relying on dated techniques and the practical benefits of newer AI-assisted approaches.

sections.title: Non-destructive workflow and history-based painting
sections.description: Deep dive into non-destructive editing. Introduces history states, the history brush, and the evolution from clone-based workflows to a history-paint-based approach, including saving multiple versions and how to remix edits later.

sections.title: Warping tools overview
sections.description: Demonstrates how warp tools bend perspective and space, including using adaptive wide angle to simulate extreme focal lengths and the rule of trapezoids to mimic wide-angle distortion.

sections.title: Diffusion, color adjustments, and selective color depth
concepts: Selective Color depth and color separation
sections.description: Covers diffusion-based softening techniques, color adjustments that preserve or alter mood, and a detailed walkthrough of selective color for targeted color manipulation and color separation effects.

sections.title: Two core painting tools: History Paint and Clone Paint
sections.description: Introduces two user-created painting workflows. History Paint leverages historical states for painting edits, while Clone Paint represents the narrator’s unique, earlier-created technique for painting edits across layers and history states.
